title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Marisol Nguyen
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines standards and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is consistent, high-quality, easily consumable content that reduces time-to-first-success for customers and internal teams, and decreases support load for the SDK/APIs.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Provide a single, actionable reference for producing and maintaining developer-facing docs and support artifacts.
- Scope: All public and internal SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, API examples, and doc-site operations owned by the DevEx team. Excludes ad-hoc internal notes and meeting minutes.

Owners and reviewers:

- Primary owner: DevEx Documentation (engineering)
- Day-to-day author: Marisol Nguyen
- Reviewers: Ben Carter (SDK lead), Diane Lopez (Product Docs), Ravi Patel (SRE)

Standards and conventions (high-level):

1) Content style
- Use clear headings and short intro paragraphs per Confluence style.
- Write full sentences; keep examples minimal and runnable.
- Include ownership, SLOs, and related pages at top of each doc.
- Use code fences for CLI and SDK samples.

2) File and page naming
- Short, descriptive, hyphenated names: e.g. "sdk-python-quickstart-authentication.json"
- Titles should start with the artifact type: "SDK Guide — Python: Authentication"

3) Metadata
- Every page must include: title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated (as per agents.md).
- Add labels for searchability: platform, language (python/node/go), topic (auth, streaming, embeddings).

Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow):

1) Draft → Review → Publish
- Draft: Author creates a Confluence page in the draft space, follows template.
- Review: Assign 2 reviewers (one SDK owner + one product or SRE reviewer). Reviews should be completed within 48 business hours.
- Publish: After approval, change status to published and tag release notes entry.

2) Content freeze and emergency fixes
- Minor edits: can be published directly if they are typo fixes or example corrections.
- Major changes (API contract changes, breaking behavior): create a PR, coordinate with SDK owners and Product (min 5 business day notice).
- Emergency hotfix: If documentation misleads production customers (security or outage impact), file an incident and patch doc within 4 hours; notify docs-incident Slack channel.

3) CI checks for docs (automated)
- Linting: frontmatter/metadata presence, labels, and heading depth enforced by the docs linter.
- Link check: CI runs a link-checker on merged pages; broken links open a ticket assigned to the page owner.

SDK guides (structure & required sections):

All SDK guide pages must include the following sections in this order:
- Title and short description (1–2 lines)
- TL;DR code example (runnable)
- Prerequisites and install (pip/npm/go get; minimum supported versions)
- Authentication examples (API key, environment variables, KMS notes for Private customers)
- Quick usage patterns (sync, async, streaming where applicable)
- Error handling and retry guidance (with sample error payloads)
- Performance tips (batching, concurrency, token accounting)
- Troubleshooting and common support issues (link to canonical fixes)
- Ownership and support contact (team + Slack channel)

Example TL;DR (Python):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
response = client.text.generate(model='redwood-v1', prompt='Write a haiku about latency')
print(response.text)
```

Quickstarts & templates (boilerplates and recommended repo layout):

- Quickstarts should get a user from 0 → running in under 10 minutes. Each quickstart must include: README, minimal code example, .env.example for credentials, and a short video or GIF if the flow is non-trivial.
- Repository template layout (recommended):
  - quickstart/
    - README.md
    - src/ (language-specific)
    - tests/ (smoke tests)
    - .env.example
    - LICENSE

- Cookiecutter/template variables: project_name, language, model_choice, streaming (true|false), sample_prompts. Keep templates under the devex-templates GitHub org and add a release tag when updating a template.

API examples (canonical examples and patterns):

- Maintain a curated set of API examples for common patterns: text generation (simple + streaming), chat with system messages, embeddings, batch inference, function calling, and error handling.
- Each example must include:
  - One-line description
  - Minimal curl example (for reproducibility)
  - One example per officially-supported SDK (Python, Node.js, Go)

Example curl: authentication + streaming (line-oriented)

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain KV caching"}]}'

Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list):

This section captures the highest-volume issues DevEx and Support see, with standardized fixes and links to relevant docs and examples. Owners must keep this section up-to-date; SRE and Support productize fixes as runbooks when they impact production.

1) "Invalid API key" error (400/401)
- Symptom: 401s returned from SDKs or curl.
- Canonical fix: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY set and does not include surrounding quotes; ensure correct project/region in headers.
- Commands/checks:
  - `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` (ensure not blank)
  - `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`
- Page to link: SDK auth guide (auth section)

2) Streaming responses truncated / reconnects
- Symptom: Partial events or sudden connection close on streaming routes.
- Root causes: network proxies (NGINX timeout), client-side read timeouts, or model-side preemption under capacity pressure.
- Canonical fixes:
  - Increase proxy timeouts and turn off request buffering (nginx: proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_buffering off).
  - Use official SDK streaming helpers (they handle reconnection logic).
  - If model preemption suspected, route to compatible fallback model via smart routing (see routing docs).
- Owner: Runtime + DevEx

3) High token usage / unexpected cost spikes
- Symptom: Customers report higher-than-expected token bill.
- Canonical fix: Check prompts for unbounded system messages, loops, or repeated calls. Enable per-request max_tokens and set stop sequences. Use batching and caching (prefix KV caching).
- Commands/checks:
  - Check recent requests via Console filter by API key and route; export token histogram.
  - Recommend quantization profile or model variant for cost-sensitive workloads.

4) Non-deterministic outputs after SDK upgrade
- Symptom: Customers observe output regressions after an SDK or model version bump.
- Canonical fix: Reproduce with exact model + tokenizer versions; pin model versions in the client; attach prompt/eval to regression-triage.
- Process: Create a regression report, include seed prompts, model ID, SDK version, and call stack. Notify Applied ML and Ramp rollout if high-severity.

Publishing templates and example PR checklist:

- Include metadata and labels.
- Provide a TL;DR and minimal runnable example.
- Add smoke test (CI) that runs one minimal example.
- Add screenshots or GIF if UI elements are involved.
- Add a release notes bullet if this changes user-visible behavior.

Operational metrics and SLOs for DevEx docs:

- Review SLA: 48 business hours for initial review.
- Hotfix SLA: 4 hours from incident filed for critical doc errors.
- Documentation coverage target: 95% of public SDK surface has at least one example.
- Support reduction target: 15% lower "getting started" tickets year-over-year measured by tag in zendesk.

Maintenance and cadence:

- Quarterly doc audits: each owner reviews pages and updates for accuracy.
- Major SDK release: update SDK guide and at least one quickstart before shipping GA.

Common templates and quick links (resources):

- DevEx templates repo: https://github.com/redwood/devex-templates
- Quickstart canonical examples: https://github.com/redwood/quickstarts
- Docs site linter and CI instructions: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-linter-ops (internal)

Appendix — Example doc template (copy into new pages):

Title: SDK Guide — <Language>: <Topic>
Description: One sentence summary.
Owner: <team-or-person>
Status: draft|in_review|published
Labels: language:<language>, topic:<topic>, sdk

Sections to fill:
1) TL;DR example
2) Install and auth
3) Minimal usage
4) Advanced usage (streaming, batching)
5) Error handling and troubleshooting
6) Related pages and support links

If you have questions about this playbook or need edits to process, ping #devex-docs or email devex-docs@redwood.ai.
